title: Overhead Press
summary: A standing barbell press overhead for the front delts and triceps, with core and upper-trap work.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for front delts (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.6 for triceps (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.5 for side delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly side delts total.
Library rating 0.3 for traps (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.2 for abs: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly abs total.
Library rating 0.15 for obliques: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly obliques total.

setup.text: Start with the bar on your front shoulders, your hands just outside shoulder width, and your glutes and abs tight.
Press straight up, moving your head back slightly so the bar can pass.
Finish with the bar over your mid-foot and your head through between your arms.
Lower under control back to your shoulders.

form_cues.cue: Squeeze glutes and brace your abs
Move your head back as the bar passes your face
Finish with the bar over mid-foot
Squeeze your glutes so you don't lean back into the lift.

mistakes.text: Leaning back hard and turning it into an incline press.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where you can fail a rep safely, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
